title: DNA says Pompeii's 'mother' was a man
description:
A Pompeii victim found in 1974 wearing a gold bracelet, beside a small child, was long described as a mother. A 2024 ancient DNA study found this person was genetically male, with no sign of relation to the child (up to the third degree). Two victims found close together in 1914, read as an embrace and imagined as sisters or a mother and daughter: the one who could be tested was male. The casts were made from 1863 on by pouring plaster into the voids the bodies left in the ash, and restorers reworked some of them over the years, possibly to tell a story. The DNA does not say who these people were; it shows the old stories were guesses.

Source:
- Pilli et al. 2024, "Ancient DNA challenges prevailing interpretations of the Pompeii plaster casts", Current Biology 34(22), 5307-5318. doi:10.1016/j.cub.2024.10.007

Images: Pompeii photographs by F.-E. Le Dien (c. 1853) and A.-N. Normand (1851), The Metropolitan Museum of Art, public domain.

Narration: Kokoro-82M synthetic voice. Illustrated animation; the bracelet, corridor, casting diagram and restoration scene are illustrative, not to scale.
